title: Continuous cohomology commutes with unions of finite submodules
statement: Let $G$ be a profinite group, $\ell$ a prime, and $M$ a discrete continuous $\ell$-primary $G$-module. Let $\{M_i\}$ be the directed system of all finite $G$-stable submodules of $M$, ordered by inclusion; it has union $M$. For every integer $q\geq0$, the canonical map $\varinjlim_i H^q(G,M_i)\to H^q(G,M)$ for continuous cohomology (computed by the continuous cochain complex in [def-exc-continuous-cohomology]) is an isomorphism.

proof.text: For every n, the coefficient module of continuous n-cochains satisfies $\operatorname{Cont}(G^n,M)=\varinjlim_i\operatorname{Cont}(G^n,M_i)$. Indeed, $G^n$ is compact and $M$ is discrete, so a continuous cochain has finite image. Each value has an open stabilizer, hence a finite G-orbit; the G-stable submodule generated by the finitely many values is therefore finite and is contained in some $M_i$. This proves surjectivity onto the cochain colimit. If two cochains become equal in $M$, their finitely many values agree in one common finite stable submodule because the index system is directed, proving injectivity. These identifications commute with the cochain differentials by equivariance and additivity.

Taking cohomology of the compatible cochain complexes in Step 1 commutes with the filtered colimit: kernels and images in each degree commute with this colimit by exactness of filtered colimits of abelian groups [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-abelian-groups-exact]. Thus the colimit of the degree-q cohomology groups of the finite submodules is canonically the degree-q cohomology of the colimit complex. The latter is $H^q(G,M)$ by the continuous-cochain computation in [def-exc-continuous-cohomology], giving the asserted canonical isomorphism.
